timeline_reviews.summary: Transport stream for the serial run; semantic evidence is projected into the single raw agent trajectory.
Serial parent trajectory: single-agent probing, project skeleton/source creation, and timeout before complete implementation.

parallel.requirements: The run recognized it had to reverse-engineer the provided genact executable from CLI behavior and documentation only, without source-code lookup or wrapping.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It built shared probing tools and a guide, then delegated all 21 modules to workflow children and launched a separate CLI subagent while the parent continued experiments.
parallel.implementation: Most observable work was sampling, parsing, timing probes, and research notes. The module workflow asked children to write Rust modules, but no final Rust crate source reached the submitted artifact.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Delivery was not assembled into a new buildable project; the artifact included tools, research captures, gifs, README, .git, LICENSE, and the original executable, with artifact validation marked not ok.
parallel.verification: The parallel run performed extensive behavioral probes but no integrated compile/test of an assembled replacement occurred before closure; official evaluation compile_failed with all 237 tests not run.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow was killed with many module children still in progress/start and one child in error, leaving delegated module work unrecovered and the final package not a valid replacement implementation.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same cleanroom reverse-engineering task and the prohibition on source-code lookup, binary analysis, and wrapping the original executable.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent probed CLI behavior and modules, then personally created a Rust project skeleton instead of delegating ownership to subagents.
serial.implementation: It created Cargo.toml, compile.sh, src/term.rs, src/rng.rs, src/cli.rs, and src/io.rs, implementing part of the CLI/output foundation but not the full module set.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Its artifact packaging succeeded and included the Rust source skeleton and compile script, but the source tree was incomplete and still did not build successfully under the official evaluator.
serial.verification: The run compared many CLI outputs and timing behaviors, but there is no final integrated passing build/test loop before timeout; official evaluation also compile_failed with 237 tests not run.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial attempt timed out before creating enough module implementations and project glue for a compilable complete reimplementation, despite having a cleaner deliverable tree than parallel.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the cleanroom behavioral-reimplementation task and documented no web/source/wrapping constraints in its guide.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and investigated behavior under the same cleanroom restrictions.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no material requirement-recognition difference; both knew the goal, but parallel converted it into delegated per-module work while serial kept a local implementation focus.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work across a 21-module workflow plus a separate CLI subagent and expected child agents to produce module specs, data files, and Rust modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegation and kept ownership in the parent, later creating the project skeleton itself.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's decomposition put required implementation behind child completion, while serial directly owned the evolving codebase despite covering less behavior overall.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel gave children a shared guide, fixed paths, module function signature, data naming, and import conventions for generated module/data files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial maintained all observations and interface decisions inside one trajectory while writing core source files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The available evidence supports adequate initial interface context in parallel; the failure is not an interface contract dispute but the absence of recovered child output after cancellation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel mostly produced probes, helper scripts, and research captures before launching module workers; the submitted tree did not contain the Rust implementation files expected by the workflow brief.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial created a std-only Rust crate skeleton with CLI, RNG, terminal, and IO modules before timing out.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete artifact difference is that serial delivered partial source code, whereas parallel delivered research/tooling and the original executable without a buildable replacement source tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow result remained null and status killed, with one module child in error and many children still in progress or only started when the run closed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join; partial work remained in the parent-controlled workspace and package.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost delegated required work at a child-result lifecycle boundary; serial's incompleteness was local unfinished implementation rather than unreturned child work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used shared /workspace and /tmp research artifacts, but no completed child implementation was integrated into a final crate before packaging.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote directly into the final source tree, and the packaged artifact includes Cargo.toml, compile.sh, and source modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material integration difference is absence of assembly in parallel versus partial direct assembly in serial; no concrete concurrent overwrite is proven.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel conducted many behavior probes, but the workflow brief explicitly told module children not to compile and no final integrated compile/test is evident before the killed closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also performed extensive probes and checked environment constraints, but did not reach an integrated successful compile before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both lacked evaluator-aligned acceptance evidence and both compile-failed; parallel additionally lost delegated module work before any integrated verification stage could use it.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel exhausted the 2400-second cell budget after launching a high-breadth workflow, with workflow state killed and numerous children unfinished.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also hit the 2400-second budget, but its timeout occurred after local source-file creation rather than after a failed child workflow return.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The official outcome was the same, but the closure mode differed: parallel closed with unrecovered delegated work and an invalid artifact, while serial closed with partial code packaged correctly.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both runs officially failed: the current completed evaluation for each reports compile_failed and all 237 tests not run. The important task-solving difference is not a discordant pass/fail result. Parallel delegated module implementation to a workflow that was killed before results could be joined or replaced, so its artifact was research/tooling plus the original executable and was marked artifact-invalid. Serial stayed single-agent, created a Rust crate skeleton and packaged it successfully, but still timed out before completing enough implementation to compile.
parallel_contributors: Required module implementation was delegated to a large workflow that ended killed with result null and unfinished children.
The submitted parallel artifact did not contain the Rust source tree requested by the workflow brief and was artifact_validation ok=false.
serial_contributors: Serial maintained implementation ownership locally and created Cargo.toml, compile.sh, and several Rust source files.
Serial packaging was artifact_validation ok=true, but the project remained incomplete and compile_failed.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts spent extensive time empirically probing many genact modules and did not finish the complete reimplementation.
Serial's failure appears to be ordinary incompleteness of a partial Rust implementation, while parallel's worse artifact shape follows from unresolved delegated workflow work.
evaluator_effects: The official evaluator reported compile_failed for both modes and therefore did not run any of the 237 tests in either attempt.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported comparative contributors to different failed deliverables

candidates.reason: Rejected: the active children were lost through workflow/cell abortion; the more specific retained defect is no takeover of failed or cancelled required child work before closure.

The parallel parent delegated required module implementation to a 21-agent workflow, the workflow ended killed with one child in error and many still in progress/start, and the parent never resumed, reassigned, or completed that unfinished scope before closure.
candidates.realized_consequence: The required child-owned module work was not recovered or assembled; the submitted artifact contains research/tooling and the original executable rather than a buildable replacement source tree, leading to compile_failed.
candidates.near_match_reason: The broad fan-out and budget pressure are real, but they are downstream of the same killed-workflow episode; correcting the missing takeover/resume boundary is the specific intervention that would change this episode.

Rejected: no broad cleanup/rebuild/promotion overwrote a current final tree and invalidated another agent's work.

Rejected: shared generated sample files were intentionally provided as research inputs, and no contaminating consumption caused wrong execution or verification.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Early Child Termination, Late Finalization, Missing Implementation Join, Unused Completed Result, and Blind Timeout Wait were considered but not retained because they would restate the same killed workflow/no-takeover chain or require completed/available results not present here.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; the only retained coordination pattern with a realized adverse consequence is the failed/cancelled workflow with no takeover.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: The review keeps one pair-level occurrence for the single result-lifecycle/failure-propagation chain and rejects downstream fan-out, timing, join, monitoring, and write symptoms without separate episodes.
